goal: A gate-first, engine-independent Go core that turns a GitHub issue into a gated pull request and addresses human review feedback on that pull request, behind a pluggable Runner interface. The agent proposes; it never merges and holds no deploy credential.
progress: Both core loops ship and are dogfooded. Issue-to-PR (loop.Run) produced a merged dependency-upgrade PR on charlesgreen/gsm. Fix-on-request (loop.Fix, `simplycubed address`) is built and tested end to end against a real git repo and bare remote. The codex-on-Azure adapter is real; the whole loop still tests with no model behind the fake Runner.
invariants: claude-proposes-actions-dispose: the loop only ever opens or updates a pull request; it never merges and holds no deploy credential.
gate-first: no change is proposed until the repo's own gate passes, and `make check` is green at every commit.
gate-required: a target repo with no `gate:` configured is refused.
engine-independence: the loop, gate, config, state machine, roles, and domain types compile and test without any real model call, behind the Runner interface with a deterministic fake.
untrusted-input-delimited: issue bodies and review feedback are delimited as data, never treated as instructions, and the role bounds win over them.
no-secrets-in-repo: no session-private material (host credentials, Azure resource or deployment names, keys) enters this public repository.
